items.description:
PEP is a nationwide value retailer selling affordable clothing, footwear and homeware, along with in-store cellular contracts and other financial services such as money transfers and airtime top-ups. It is one of South Africa's largest single-brand retail chains, and the Delft Mall branch carries the same core range of everyday clothing and household basics sold at PEP stores across the country.

This store trades from Shop 32 in Delft Mall, on the corner of Hindle Road and Delft Main Road in Delft. It suits shoppers looking for low-priced clothing and household essentials, along with a quick cellular or financial transaction, without needing to travel outside the area.

items.description:
Plush Bazaar is a hiring shop and food studio at The Old Biscuit Mill in Woodstock, Cape Town. Its second-floor loft space has a variety of textured walls and backgrounds, and it describes itself as Cape Town's newest hiring shop with an expertly curated retail section. The studio also has a well-equipped kitchen for food styling and shoots.

Its earlier blog, written as Plush Props, describes the space as a place for stylists, wedding planners and event organisers to hire, buy, cook and shoot props. Shooting can be done on site, which speeds up the turnaround from the pot to the camera. It suits stylists, planners and anyone who needs props or a styled shoot handled in one studio.

items.description:
Silulo Ulutho Technologies is a technology outlet at Khayelitsha Mall, part of a company established in 2004 with its head office in Cape Town. The company describes its mission as bridging the digital divide through accessible technology education and community empowerment, and it is black owned.

Its services include computer training, internet access, printing services, CV writing and business ICT support, offered at branches across the Eastern and Western Cape. The group says it is driven by technology, accessibility, empowerment and education. It suits people in Khayelitsha who need computer access, training, printing or help with a CV close to home.

items.description:
St Francis Veterinary Clinic is a veterinary practice in Bergvliet providing general consultations and everyday health care for cats, dogs and other companion animals. Customer reviews describe a team that is friendly and efficient, willing to fit in an appointment at short notice when a pet needs urgent attention, and an in-clinic shop stocked with pet-care products for owners to pick up after a visit.

The practice is on Main Road in Bergvliet, trading through the week with shorter hours over the weekend for owners who need a Saturday or Sunday consultation. It suits pet owners in the southern suburbs looking for a local clinic for routine check-ups, ongoing care, or an unplanned visit when their animal needs attention.

Swimmattix Swim School is an internationally accredited swim school with a branch in Sherwood Shopping Centre in Bergvliet, Cape Town. It teaches swimming to children from a young age through to adults, and its site says it is open every day of the week.

The school runs a 'fetch & teach' programme for schools, and parent testimonials on its site describe children who are eager for their next lesson and who have become confident, safe swimmers within months of starting. The school suits families who want structured swimming lessons for children of any age, from toddlers to older kids and adults.

The Good Food Cafe operates inside Merrypak's premises in Ndabeni, trading alongside the packaging and craft retailer's own shop and its in-house print and copy counter. Merrypak stocks boxes, ribbon, wrapping paper, gift accessories, stationery and other packaging and craft materials, and draws a steady flow of trade and retail customers to its Ndabeni site, giving the café a built-in base of visitors looking for something to eat during their trip.

The café shares Merrypak's address at 45 Morningside Road in Ndabeni. It suits customers calling in for packaging supplies, along with Merrypak's own staff, who want a casual stop for food and refreshments without leaving the premises.

items.description:
The Palms Pub & Grill is a family-friendly restaurant on Bottelary Road in Brackenfell, Cape Town, and has been a local favourite since 2009. The menu includes burgers, fall-off-the-bone eisbein and wood-fired pizzas, alongside quicker lunches, and the restaurant also runs food specials through the week.

Its bar serves gin, wine and classic cocktails such as rum and coke, and the site describes the team as ready to pour a drink worth staying for. The Palms also shows live sports and has a dedicated kids' area, according to its site. It suits families and groups in Brackenfell who want a relaxed pub-style meal with drinks and entertainment.

items.description:
The President Hotel is a hotel in Bantry Bay, Cape Town, with views of the Atlantic and Table Mountain. Its rooms are designed for easy stays, with options looking out over the ocean, the mountain or the city, and guests can book directly through the hotel's own site for its best rate.

The hotel describes its rooms as a place to settle in, unwind and take in the scenery after a day out, with room service available in the evening. Its site lists stay, wellness, dining and offer sections for guests planning a visit. It suits visitors who want sea or mountain views without leaving central Cape Town.

The Spot is a barber shop at 98 Main Road in Mowbray, Cape Town. Its services include the Blade Fade, the Style Cut combining a haircut and beard trim, Gents and College cuts, Kids cuts, Pensioners cuts and a standalone beard trim.

Its Full House package combines a haircut, beard trim and hot towel treatment for a complete visit. The barbershop's profile describes it as a refreshing stop in a bustling town for anyone who wants a sharp haircut or a precise beard trim, with a commitment to style and satisfaction. Clients can book through its Fresha page. It suits men and boys of any age in Mowbray who want a quick, well-priced cut.

items.description:
Vadivelu is a modern Indian restaurant on Kloof Street in Gardens, built around the Tamil heritage of the family behind it. The dining room is decorated with sage and terracotta walls, jungle-print wallpaper and pistachio banquettes, with a deep verandah warmed by patio heaters and a log fire inside for cooler evenings.

The kitchen draws on Southern Indian streetfood and home cooking, serving dishes such as potato masala dosa with coconut chutney, pani puri curry bombs, prawn tikka bites, prawn coconut curry, aloo gobi and lamb tikka masala with parathas, alongside a short wine list and a strong vegetarian and vegan selection. The restaurant is at 151 Kloof Street in Gardens. It suits diners wanting a buzzy, modern take on Southern Indian food with vegetarian and vegan choices alongside the meat and seafood dishes.

items.description:
The Warrior Toy Museum is a toy museum on King George Way in Simon's Town, Cape Town. It holds a collection of around 4,000 model cars and 500 vintage dolls, the oldest of which is 165 years old, alongside two working model railways.

Its Cape Town Magazine listing says entry costs just R10, which makes it an affordable stop for visitors exploring Simon's Town. It suits collectors, families and visitors curious about vintage toys and model trains in the area. The museum is a small, old-fashioned attraction that gives visitors a close look at historical toys rather than a large modern exhibit, which suits anyone who enjoys browsing vintage collections at a relaxed pace.

items.description:
Wetton Bolt and Nut is an industrial fastener supplier at 150 Wetton Road in Wetton, Cape Town. Its range covers fasteners, tools and lubricants, and it stocks stainless steel, galvanised steel, high tensile steel and brass bolts and nuts.

Customer reviews on its directory listing describe it as having almost always what customers need when looking for bolts, nuts and related items, with good, friendly service. One reviewer notes it is one of the few suppliers open on a Saturday for these items. It suits tradespeople, workshops and DIY customers in Wetton and nearby suburbs who need fasteners and fixings close to hand.

items.description:
Aqua Spares is a motor spares business in Steenberg, Cape Town, trading since 2011. Its site lets customers search its vehicle inventory to find parts for a range of makes, and it offers fast nationwide delivery.

The business lists its trading hours as 08:00 to 17:00, and its stock includes used parts from makes such as Nissan, Toyota, Land Rover, Ford, Mercedes-Benz, Hyundai, Volkswagen and Volvo. Customers can browse the latest inventory online before visiting or ordering. It suits vehicle owners looking for new and used spares across a wide range of makes and models. The business lists current stock such as bakkies, hatchbacks and SUVs on its site, so buyers can check availability before travelling to the yard.

items.description:
Barrister's Grill is a steakhouse and pub-style restaurant in Cardiff Castle, Newlands, Cape Town. The restaurant says it has one of Cape Town's most extensive wine lists, with a selection to suit most palates, and live music plays every Sunday.

The restaurant takes bookings for office parties, 40th birthdays, baby showers and other celebrations, and guests can email to discuss a function. It does not take bookings on the deck after 12:30pm, and it is not pet friendly. It suits groups and wine lovers who want a relaxed meal with live music on a Sunday. Diners who want a quieter evening can combine a meal from the wine list with the live music lineup posted on the restaurant's site each month.

BASI Pilates Academy is a Pilates studio in Sea Point, Cape Town, offering private, semi-private and teacher training sessions. It was formerly known as Living Life Pilates, and it now trades as BASI Pilates Academy Cape Town.

Sessions are tailored for strength, recovery, mobility and long-term movement health, and the studio works with clients at different stages of their Pilates journey, from first-time visitors to aspiring teachers. The academy also delivers internationally recognised BASI teacher training from its Sea Point studio. It suits anyone wanting one-on-one or small-group Pilates, as well as people training to become Pilates teachers. Sessions are offered in a focused studio environment, and the academy's site lets new clients book an appointment directly online.

items.description:
The Black Marlin is a seafood restaurant just outside Simon's Town on the way to Cape Point, on one of the Cape's most scenic coastlines. Its menu covers seafood, poultry, meats and desserts, and the restaurant also has a wine list.

The stretch of coast near the restaurant, from Strandfontein to Cape Point, is one of South Africa's finest boat-based whale-watching areas. The Black Marlin also hosts weddings and corporate functions, from romantic gatherings to larger events. The site traces back to 1814, when Thomas Drury was granted the land that became known as Miller's Point. It suits diners who want a scenic coastal setting for a meal, a whale-watching stop or a function.

items.description:
Harry Goemans Garden Centre is a family-run nursery on Kommetjie Road in Sunnydale, Cape Town, open from 8:30am to 5pm every day. The Cafe at Harry Goemans has reopened under the name Cinnamon and Sage, trading from the same nursery.

Harry Goemans came to South Africa from Holland and opened his first nursery on Main Road, Bergvliet, in 1960, later closed in 2009. His son-in-law Henry Fenn started the Sunnydale branch in 1994, and Henry's son Jeremy now owns and runs the garden centre, which stocks indigenous and exotic plants, pots, fertilisers, tools and irrigation supplies. It suits gardeners visiting the nursery who also want a casual breakfast or lunch on site.

Cafe Nood is a cafe in Quadrant Square on Wilderness Road in Claremont, Cape Town. Underground parking is available at Library Square nearby, which makes it easy for customers to park and visit.

The cafe trades Monday to Friday from 07h00 to 16h00 and Saturdays from 08h00 to 12h00, and it is closed on public holidays. Customers can contact the cafe by phone or email for enquiries. It suits people in Claremont who want breakfast or a weekday lunch close to the Quadrant Square precinct. The cafe's contact page lists both its landline numbers, so customers can call ahead to check availability or place an order for collection.
